questions: Should the pairing be a perfect matching (i.e., every cake used exactly once) or can some cakes remain unpaired? The prompt says 'pairing up these cakes into K pairs' and 'choose 2K distinct integers', implying exactly 2K cakes are used, but does not explicitly forbid leaving some cakes unused if N > 2K.

Is the goal to maximize the sum of the pair prices, or the sum of the max of the three sums per pair? The definition is clear, but could there be confusion that the max is taken over the three sums for each pair individually, not globally?
Are the pairs ordered? That is, does swapping a_i and b_i in a pair affect the price? Since max is symmetric, it does not, but the prompt does not explicitly state that pairs are unordered.
If multiple optimal total prices exist, is any acceptable? The problem asks for 'the maximum possible total price', so any tie-breaking is fine.
Can K be zero? The constraints say 1 ≤ K, so K is at least 1.
Are the cakes distinguishable only by their triple values, or also by index? Since indices are distinct in selection, but price depends only on values, indices matter only for uniqueness.
Should the implementation handle large sums (up to 2e9) without overflow in 32-bit integers? The constraints allow values up to 1e9, so sums up to 2e9 fit in 64-bit, but not necessarily 32-bit.

Is the pairing required to be a matching in the graph sense (no cake in more than one pair)? The 'distinct integers' and 'pair up' imply that, but not explicitly stated as a constraint beyond distinctness.
